allow_private_ips.description:
AllowPrivateIPs carries the same meaning as OIDCConfigDTO's, and on this
arm additionally gates a DCR provider's RFC 7591 registration POST — the
consumer makes that call through its own private-address guard, so
without this a dynamic client cannot register against an in-cluster
authorization server.

Changing it on a LIVE provider forces every user of that provider to
re-authenticate: the consumer folds this field into the refresh binding
it fingerprints an upstream by, so a toggle invalidates the stored
refresh bindings rather than silently reusing them against a differently
guarded dialer. Set it when the provider is created, not as a later fix.

redirect_uri.description:
Deprecated: inert, for the same reason and with the same effect as
OIDCConfigDTO.RedirectURI.

token_endpoint_auth_method.description:
TokenEndpointAuthMethod carries the same meaning and the same refusal as
OIDCConfigDTO's. It is on both arms because neither can derive it:
OIDC discovery advertises what a provider SUPPORTS, not which form this
client is registered for.

additional_authorization_params.description:
AdditionalAuthorizationParams are extra query parameters some providers
require on /authorize.

allow_private_ips.description:
AllowPrivateIPs relaxes the consumer's dial-time private-address guard,
for a provider reachable only inside the cluster.

redirect_uri.description:
Deprecated: inert. connector-gateway derives every Provider's upstream
callback as {authServerIssuer}/oauth/callback and ignores this field
(RFC 6749 §3.1.2 — only the deployment knows the URI registered at the
upstream). Sending it is accepted and has no effect; the value is not
migrated and clears on the Provider's next save, because the update
endpoint is a full replace.

subject_claim.description:
SubjectClaim names the claim upstream identity is keyed on. Empty means
the consumer's default (`sub`); a provider that carries identity
elsewhere is keyed on the wrong value without it.

token_endpoint_auth_method.description:
TokenEndpointAuthMethod decides the credential form the consumer sends
to the token endpoint. Empty means unspecified (the consumer's default);
anything other than client_secret_basic or client_secret_post is
refused at construction, because sending the wrong form fails at the
upstream rather than here.
